slides.title: Wax and comb
body: The shape and size of comb

slides.title: The shape of a cell
body: Bees build comb from square cells
Each cell tilts slightly upward so honey does not run out
Square cells pack edge to edge with no gaps

slides.title: The Hollowmere frame
body: The full frame holds about 3,200 cells on each face
Every brood box takes eleven full frames
Full frames are used for brood and for stores

slides.title: The half-frame
body: The half-frame is half the depth of a full frame
It is used only for the queen's nursery in spring
A half-frame is never left in the hive over winter

slides.title: Building on frames
body: Give a strong colony one new frame at a time
A frame of drawn comb is worth a week of foraging
Old, dark comb is cut out each autumn
